title: Union workers and drivers rally against robotaxis in Washington

tea.why: Union workers, drivers, and religious leaders are protesting against a legislative proposal to introduce commercial robotaxis in D.C.
tea.want: Protesters urged the D.C. council to reject the Autonomous Vehicle Deployment Authorization Amendment Act of 2026.
tea.changed: Oct 10: Union workers, drivers, and religious leaders rallied outside the John Wilson Building against autonomous vehicles.

summary: Union workers, drivers, and religious leaders gathered outside the John Wilson Building in Washington, D.C., to protest against a legislative proposal allowing autonomous vehicles to operate commercially in the city. As D.C. council members met to discuss the Autonomous Vehicle Deployment Authorization Amendment Act of 2026, demonstrators urged the council to reject the legislation. Participants argued that the introduction of robotaxis would displace rideshare drivers, eliminate jobs, and take food from families' tables. The legislation, introduced in May by Councilmember Charles Allen, would establish a commercial autonomous vehicle program run by the District Department of Transportation.
demands: Reject the Autonomous Vehicle Deployment Authorization Amendment Act of 2026
Protect driving jobs from being displaced by robotaxis
response: No official response reported in the sources.
